A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PC-CLIP and comparative prompting. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite appendix reordering and substantial experimental additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original difference-based and zeroshot classification experiments, embedding analyses, image-generation results, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original retrieval, captioning, synthetic-data quality, robustness, linear-probing, and model-scale evaluations.

M1.justification: The main contrastive objective, comparison-generation procedure, and comparative-prompting rule remain unchanged. Appendix C.6 adds an evaluated full-finetuning variant that also updates the image encoder for linear probing, whereas v1's experiments update only the text encoder.

E1.justification: V2 adds Flickr30k image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval, Spot-the-Difference captioning and text-to-image-pair retrieval, and ImageNet-A/ImageNet-R distribution-shift evaluations. These substantially expand actual task and test-distribution coverage beyond the retained classification and generation experiments.

E2.justification: The original CLIP, COCO-finetuned CLIP, and Rewrite-finetuned CLIP comparisons remain. New Tables 12–13 add IDC + CLIP and the reported IFDC and VACC reference baselines against IDC + PC-CLIP; the latter reference scores are taken from prior work. This is a localized expansion for image-difference tasks.

E3.justification: Table 5 replaces CLIPScore with GPT-4o-mini ratings on a 1–5 scale. Added protocols include retrieval and captioning metrics, a 300-example synthetic-data audit, linear probes using 100 labeled instances per class, and ViT-H/14 evaluations. Table 5 changes its image count from 8000 to 800, but v1 Appendix D.1 already specified 800, so an actual sample reduction is not established. V2 Appendix D.1 also retains the old CLIPScore description.

E4.justification: V2 adds filtering/noise ablation, natural distribution-shift tests, encoder assessment through linear probing, larger-model evaluation, confidence-versus-prompting-gain analysis, and a synthetic-data quality audit. These address robustness, mechanism, and applicability questions beyond the retained COCO-versus-CUB and contrastive-versus-MSE ablations.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 adds statistical estimation of the correlation between classifier confidence and comparative-prompting gains across five datasets. Existing five-seed mean-plus-standard-error reporting is retained. No confidence interval or significance test accompanies the new correlation.

E6.justification: Original classification, embedding-distance, and loss/data-ablation values are retained. New results include Flickr30k text-to-image R@1 of 64.88 for CLIP versus 69.80 for PC-CLIP, and captioning CIDEr of 41.17 versus 43.09 for their IDC variants. Tables 14–17 add filtering, shift, probing, and scale results. Table 5 replaces CLIPScore values 0.532/0.542 with judge scores 1.75/2.33; these different metrics do not establish a cross-version performance gain.

T1.justification: The objectives and mathematical definitions in Equations (1)–(5), including difference-based classification and comparative prompting, are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: V2's introduction explicitly extends the claimed benefits to cross-modal retrieval, particularly text-to-image retrieval. The central contributions of comparison-based finetuning, comparative prompting, classification improvements, and embedding arithmetic remain substantially unchanged in the abstract and discussion.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking prompting benefits to low confidence, synthetic-comparison errors to missing caption details, and limited visual-feature gains to predominantly text-encoder benefits. It also argues robustness to noisy comparisons and applicability at larger scales. These refine the earlier explanations and limitations without replacing their central interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendices B.3–B.4 add exact judging prompts, inputs, and scoring rubrics; Section 4.4 specifies 77-token retrieval truncation. Existing hyperparameters, compute disclosures, and code access remain. However, v2 removes v1's explicit SDXL two-encoder replacement description and names ViT-G/14 instead of ViT-L/14, leaving the generation setup less clearly reconciled.

R1.justification: Related work adds targeted discussion of image-difference captioning, citing Jhamtani and Berg-Kirkpatrick, Park, Guo, and Hu, and distinguishes PC-CLIP as incorporating differences into embeddings. References also expand for new benchmarks and comparators, while OpenCLIP and eDiff-I citations disappear. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: Most original prose and method exposition are retained, with localized clarifications, an added prompting example, and acknowledgments. Appendices A–C are reordered from generation/experiments/details to details/generation/experiments, and new experimental subsections are inserted. This is a limited narrative revision rather than a comprehensive rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adopts TMLR typography and page layout, enlarges and relocates retained displays, and introduces boxed prompts. It adds seven experimental tables and a synthetic-quality histogram, while revising Table 5's metric label and caption. The original qualitative generation grids are retained and renumbered, not newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical validation through retrieval and image-difference tasks, while the synthetic-data audit and filtering ablation directly examine previously weakly tested supervision-quality assumptions. Probing, scale, and shift evaluations further establish the approach's scope. These gains outweigh localized reporting weaknesses, including inconsistent image-generation metric/encoder descriptions and occasional overstatements of mixed results in the new tables.
